claims.text: A machine-learning interatomic potential can enable efficient molecular-dynamics simulations.
The potential should be trained on DFT data for both solid and liquid configurations near melting.
Two-phase coexistence or interface-pinning simulations using the potential can accurately predict melting temperature.
The proposed simulations can predict the enthalpy and entropy of fusion.
The proposed simulations can predict the volume change at the melting point.
A high-melting refractory solid near its melting point can be represented with coexisting solid and liquid regions in the proposed simulation.
The expensive ab initio thermodynamic-integration process is to be replaced by simulations using a DFT-trained machine-learning interatomic potential.
The simulations will use two-phase coexistence or interface-pinning methods near the melting temperature.
Machine-learning potentials can achieve accuracy near that of their underlying DFT calculations.
The machine-learning potential accurately captures interactions in both solid and liquid phases.
Training on DFT-calculated energies and forces retains near-ab-initio accuracy for configurations relevant to melting.
Phase-coexistence or interface-pinning simulations permit efficient extraction of melting properties.
The proposed framework bypasses the high computational cost of full ab initio thermodynamic integration.
Predicted melting properties will have error margins comparable to DFT-based predictions.
The proposed framework will operate at a fraction of the computational cost of DFT-based calculations.
Conventional ab initio free-energy calculations based on thermodynamic integration and ab initio molecular dynamics are accurate but computationally prohibitive for high-throughput studies.
Accuracy depends on the quality and transferability of the machine-learning potential.
Predictions may deviate from DFT benchmarks at pressures, compositions, or other conditions substantially outside the training regime.
Generalization across all relevant high-temperature phase configurations remains uncertain and requires validation.
Deviation of more than approximately 5–10% from DFT or experimental reference values would falsify the proposed accuracy claim.
